it still had the power of the old times. There was, for instance, the
thing that seemed to me most beautiful in it. It was not the grey
hills, or the green valleys, or even the dark and solemn woods; but
the village, which was the only part of the landscape that is not in any
sense a land of dreams, but a land of dreams. It was the same village
that I had known in my childhood, the same village of grey cottages and
red roofs, the same village of village shops and village pubs. I can
still see the village of my memories so vividly in the mind that I seem
to have actually returned. But I have not returned. I have been to
that town, and I have found it to be much changed.

In the old days the town was in a far more deserted state than it is
now; its streets were not so clean, its shops so small, and its houses
